domain_guidance.summary: This domain focuses on the management of respiratory conditions within critical care settings, including the application of advanced respiratory support and monitoring techniques for patients with acute lung issues and complex respiratory failure.

This domain covers general critical care principles, including the assessment and stabilization of patients with multi-system involvement and the coordination of care in the intensive care unit to ensure optimal patient outcomes.

editorial.overview: The NBRC RRT-ACCS Adult Critical Care Specialist exam is administered by the NBRC to assess clinical proficiency in critical care environments. The assessment covers two primary domains: Respiratory Critical Care and General Critical Care. It is a 240-minute exam consisting of 150 questions, designed to verify that respiratory therapists possess the knowledge required to manage patients in high-acuity settings effectively and safely within a hospital environment.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the official NBRC exam guide to understand the structure of the 150 questions. Focus your study on the two domains: Respiratory Critical Care and General Critical Care. Use clinical resources to practice patient management scenarios. Ensure you are familiar with the 240-minute time limit by taking practice tests that simulate the actual exam environment to build your confidence and readiness for the assessment.
editorial.who_should_take: This exam is intended for respiratory therapists who work in adult critical care units. Candidates should have clinical experience in managing complex respiratory conditions and providing advanced life support in various hospital environments.
